sn2.7:1.2: This saying by Pañcālacaṇḍa is quoted by Udāyī and explained by Ānanda at [an9.42](). Pañcālacaṇḍa makes an appearance at [dn32:10.16]() alongside Āḷavaka, the tutelary deity of Āḷavī, hinting that he may be the fierce (_caṇḍa_) protector of the Pañcāla clan. Several Pañcālacaṇḍas appear in [ja536]() and [ja546](). A Pañcālacaṇḍa appears as a Vedic teacher of the idea that speech is what unifies (Aitereya Āraṇyaka 3.1.6 = Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka 7.19, Gopatha Brāhmaṇa 1.1.27n).
sn2.7:2.3: The compound _jhānamabujjhi_ can be resolved as either _jhānaṁ abujjhi_ (“understood absorption”) or _jhānena abujjhi_ (“awakened by means of absorption”). The explanation at [an9.42]() emphasizes that each of the stages of absorption is itself still a “confinement”, and only Nibbāna is the opening. This suggests that the thrust of the verse is that even the refined consciousness of absorption must be surmounted, supporting the sense “understood absorption”.
